title: Should Homework Be Abolished?
text:
Many educators argue that homework should be abolished, claiming it increases stress without improving learning. Supporters of this view point to studies suggesting that the benefits of homework are small for younger children. They also note that students from poorer households often lack a quiet place to study, which widens the gap between pupils.

Nevertheless, a complete ban would be a mistake. Regular practice helps students consolidate what they have learned in class, and it teaches them to manage their time, a skill they will need at university and at work. The real problem, therefore, is not homework itself but poorly designed homework, which should be shorter, purposeful, and carefully matched to each pupil's level.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what do supporters of abolishing homework say about students from poorer households?
options: They often lack a quiet place to study
They receive more homework than other pupils
They perform better without any teachers

questions.text: According to the second paragraph, what skill does regular practice teach students?
Why does the author think a complete ban on homework would be a mistake?
options: Because it would stop students practising what they learned in class
Because teachers would lose their jobs

questions.text: What is the author's main position?
options: Homework should be made more purposeful rather than removed
Homework should be replaced by tests

paragraph_translations: Muchos educadores sostienen que los deberes deberían eliminarse, alegando que aumentan el estrés sin mejorar el aprendizaje. Quienes apoyan esta postura señalan estudios que sugieren que los beneficios de los deberes son escasos para los niños más pequeños. También advierten que los estudiantes de hogares más humildes a menudo carecen de un lugar tranquilo para estudiar, lo que amplía la brecha entre los alumnos.

Sin embargo, una prohibición total sería un error. La práctica regular ayuda a los estudiantes a consolidar lo aprendido en clase y les enseña a gestionar su tiempo, una habilidad que necesitarán en la universidad y en el trabajo. El verdadero problema, por tanto, no son los deberes en sí, sino los deberes mal diseñados, que deberían ser más breves, con propósito y bien ajustados al nivel de cada alumno.
